correctness.rationale: For every 0<epsilon<1 the positive circle-response change is a global diffeomorphism, and exact differentiation gives dot t=k^2 B grad H and invariant sum C. For C=0 criticality gives equality of three values g(t) with only two possible angles per level, forcing one coincident pair; the exact factor sin w(2cos w+1)(1+epsilon-2epsilon cos w) exhausts the six critical points. Explicit nonzero Hessian determinants and energy inequalities show two minima, three saddles, one maximum with only three critical energies. Compact Morse regular-level continuation gives the two-to-one number of periodic orbits. A standard-library program independently checks 1,000 phase vector/first-integral cases, 30 critical Hessians, and rational polynomial identities. These tests corroborate, not replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The recent general conservative oscillator framework emphasizes that volume conservation alone does not imply Hamiltonian dynamics or regular trajectories. This exact positive-response zero-frequency subfamily admits a global Poisson coordinate system, and a natural three-cycle leaf has a fully classified uniform critical-point and regular-periodic-orbit topology with explicit saddle threshold, rather than a local or isolated example. The precise two-to-one transition supplies structural dynamical information for a motivated oscillator family, not a generic counting exercise.
